```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

options(scipen = 999)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PURPOSE
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare the 8-wave dyadic life-satisfaction outcome data for Mplus.
#
# This file DOES NOT estimate the growth model.
#
# It:
#   1. Builds one couple-level outcome file with male and female LS at signals 0-7.
#   2. Joins the imputation-specific weights from:
#        a) locked primary entropy ATT (07b),
#        b) support-restricted entropy ATT sensitivity (08),
#        c) full-sample ATO sensitivity (08).
#   3. Exports 20 Mplus data files per specification plus TYPE=IMPUTATION
#      list files.
#   4. Leaves longitudinal outcome missingness untouched. Missing LS is coded
#      999 only at export for Mplus FIML.
#
# IMPORTANT:
# - Covariate imputation affects the weights, not the observed LS outcomes.
# - The same observed LS trajectories are therefore used in all 20 imputations.
# - No outcome values are imputed here.
# - No growth-factor variances are fixed here. Those constraints must be
#   re-evaluated in the rebuilt weighted sample rather than copied from the
#   old Mplus model.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

PARENT_PATH <- here(
  "data",
  "derived",
  "parent.rds"
)

CONTROL_PATH <- here(
  "data",
  "derived",
  "childless.rds"
)

PRIMARY_WEIGHTS_PATH <- here(
  "data",
  "derived",
  "ebal_att_datasets.rds"
)

SUPPORT_WEIGHTS_PATH <- here(
  "data",
  "derived",
  "sensitivity_rel5_age2_ebal_datasets.rds"
)

ATO_WEIGHTS_PATH <- here(
  "data",
  "derived",
  "sensitivity_ato_datasets.rds"
)

MPLUS_ROOT <- here(
  "data",
  "mplus"
)

paths_required <- c(
  PARENT_PATH,
  CONTROL_PATH,
  PRIMARY_WEIGHTS_PATH,
  SUPPORT_WEIGHTS_PATH,
  ATO_WEIGHTS_PATH
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    file.exists(
      paths_required
    )
  )
)

dir.create(
  MPLUS_ROOT,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

parent_long <- readRDS(
  PARENT_PATH
)

control_long <- readRDS(
  CONTROL_PATH
)

primary_weighted <- readRDS(
  PRIMARY_WEIGHTS_PATH
)

support_weighted <- readRDS(
  SUPPORT_WEIGHTS_PATH
)

ato_weighted <- readRDS(
  ATO_WEIGHTS_PATH
)

stopifnot(
  length(primary_weighted) == 20L,
  length(support_weighted) == 20L,
  length(ato_weighted) == 20L
)

cat("Loaded outcome grids and all three weighting specifications.\n")
```

## 1. Build the common observed outcome grid

SOEP sex coding in the rebuilt sample is `1 = male`, `2 = female`.

```{r}
outcome_long <- bind_rows(
  parent_long %>%
    mutate(group_expected = 1L),
  control_long %>%
    mutate(group_expected = 0L)
) %>%
  transmute(
    couple_id = as.character(couple_id),
    group = as.integer(group_expected),
    pid = as.numeric(pid),
    sex = as.numeric(sex),
    signal = as.integer(signal),
    syear = as.integer(syear),
    life_sat = as.numeric(life_sat)
  )

stopifnot(
  all(outcome_long$group %in% c(0L, 1L)),
  all(outcome_long$sex %in% c(1, 2)),
  all(outcome_long$signal %in% 0:7)
)

# Every person should have exactly the 8 theoretical signal positions.
person_grid_check <- outcome_long %>%
  group_by(
    couple_id,
    group,
    pid,
    sex
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_signals = n_distinct(signal),
    min_signal = min(signal),
    max_signal = max(signal),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  all(person_grid_check$n_rows == 8L),
  all(person_grid_check$n_signals == 8L),
  all(person_grid_check$min_signal == 0L),
  all(person_grid_check$max_signal == 7L)
)

# Exactly one male and one female per couple.
couple_structure_check <- outcome_long %>%
  distinct(
    couple_id,
    group,
    pid,
    sex
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    couple_id,
    group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_people = n_distinct(pid),
    n_male = sum(sex == 1),
    n_female = sum(sex == 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  all(couple_structure_check$n_people == 2L),
  all(couple_structure_check$n_male == 1L),
  all(couple_structure_check$n_female == 1L)
)

group_counts <- couple_structure_check %>%
  count(
    group,
    name = "n_couples"
  ) %>%
  arrange(group)

print(group_counts)

stopifnot(
  group_counts$n_couples[group_counts$group == 1L] == 709L,
  group_counts$n_couples[group_counts$group == 0L] == 893L
)

# Multi-group eligibility required observed LS at signal 0 for both partners.
baseline_ls_check <- outcome_long %>%
  filter(signal == 0L) %>%
  group_by(
    couple_id
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_people = n_distinct(pid),
    n_observed_ls = sum(!is.na(life_sat)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(
  all(baseline_ls_check$n_people == 2L),
  all(baseline_ls_check$n_observed_ls == 2L)
)

cat(
  "PASS: common outcome grid contains 709 parent and 893 control couples,\n",
  "with one male + one female and complete signal-0 LS for both partners.\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

## 2. Describe longitudinal outcome missingness

The multi-group sample does **not** require complete LS at signals 1–7. These missing outcome values remain missing and will be handled by Mplus under MLR/FIML.

```{r}
outcome_coverage <- outcome_long %>%
  group_by(
    group,
    sex,
    pid
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_ls = sum(!is.na(life_sat)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  count(
    group,
    sex,
    n_ls,
    name = "n_people"
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    group,
    sex,
    n_ls
  )

print(
  outcome_coverage,
  n = Inf
)

missing_by_signal <- outcome_long %>%
  group_by(
    group,
    sex,
    signal
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_observed = sum(!is.na(life_sat)),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(life_sat)),
    pct_missing = 100 * mean(is.na(life_sat)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(
  missing_by_signal,
  n = Inf
)

stopifnot(
  !any(
    outcome_coverage$n_ls == 0
  )
)
```

## 3. Convert observed outcomes to one row per couple

```{r}
male_wide <- outcome_long %>%
  filter(
    sex == 1
  ) %>%
  select(
    couple_id,
    group,
    pid,
    signal,
    life_sat
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ls_name = paste0(
      "M_LS",
      signal
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    -signal
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(
      couple_id,
      group,
      pid
    ),
    names_from = ls_name,
    values_from = life_sat
  ) %>%
  rename(
    PID_M = pid
  )

female_wide <- outcome_long %>%
  filter(
    sex == 2
  ) %>%
  select(
    couple_id,
    group,
    pid,
    signal,
    life_sat
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ls_name = paste0(
      "F_LS",
      signal
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    -signal
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(
      couple_id,
      group,
      pid
    ),
    names_from = ls_name,
    values_from = life_sat
  ) %>%
  rename(
    PID_F = pid
  )

outcome_wide <- male_wide %>%
  inner_join(
    female_wide,
    by = c(
      "couple_id",
      "group"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    couple_id
  )

expected_ls_names <- c(
  paste0("M_LS", 0:7),
  paste0("F_LS", 0:7)
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(outcome_wide) == 1602L,
  n_distinct(outcome_wide$couple_id) == 1602L,
  all(
    expected_ls_names %in%
      names(outcome_wide)
  )
)

# Stable numeric Mplus ID. This ID is for tracking only; all joins are done
# with the original string couple_id before export.
couple_key <- outcome_wide %>%
  distinct(
    couple_id
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    couple_id
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    couple_id_num = row_number()
  )

outcome_wide <- outcome_wide %>%
  left_join(
    couple_key,
    by = "couple_id"
  ) %>%
  relocate(
    couple_id_num,
    .before = couple_id
  )

saveRDS(
  outcome_wide,
  here(
    "data",
    "derived",
    "mplus_outcome_wide.rds"
  )
)

write_csv(
  couple_key,
  here(
    "data",
    "derived",
    "mplus_couple_key.csv"
  )
)

cat(
  "PASS: created one-row-per-couple observed outcome dataset.\n"
)
```

## 4. Mplus export specification

Each exported Mplus file has exactly this column order:

1. `couple_id_num`
2. `PARENT`
3. `PID_M`
4. `M_LS0` … `M_LS7`
5. `PID_F`
6. `F_LS0` … `F_LS7`
7. `WEIGHT`

Missing LS values are written as `999`.

```{r}
mplus_columns <- c(
  "couple_id_num",
  "PARENT",
  "PID_M",
  paste0(
    "M_LS",
    0:7
  ),
  "PID_F",
  paste0(
    "F_LS",
    0:7
  ),
  "WEIGHT"
)

mplus_names_text <- paste(
  mplus_columns,
  collapse = " "
)

cat(
  "Mplus column order:\n",
  mplus_names_text,
  "\n"
)
```

## 5. Helper for joining weights and exporting 20 imputations

```{r}
normalise_weight_frame <- function(
  d,
  weight_var
) {

  stopifnot(
    "couple_id" %in% names(d),
    weight_var %in% names(d)
  )

  if ("group_num" %in% names(d)) {

    group_num <-
      as.integer(
        d$group_num
      )

  } else if ("group" %in% names(d)) {

    group_num <-
      suppressWarnings(
        as.integer(
          as.character(
            d$group
          )
        )
      )

  } else {

    stop(
      "Weight dataset has neither group_num nor group."
    )
  }

  tibble(
    couple_id =
      as.character(
        d$couple_id
      ),
    group_weight =
      group_num,
    WEIGHT =
      as.numeric(
        d[[weight_var]]
      )
  )
}


export_mplus_imputations <- function(
  weight_list,
  weight_var,
  specification_name,
  expected_parent_n,
  expected_control_n
) {

  out_dir <- file.path(
    MPLUS_ROOT,
    specification_name
  )

  dir.create(
    out_dir,
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )

  stopifnot(
    length(weight_list) == 20L
  )

  export_diagnostics <- vector(
    "list",
    20L
  )

  exported_outcomes <- vector(
    "list",
    20L
  )

  file_names <- character(
    20L
  )

  for (i in seq_len(20L)) {

    weights_i <- normalise_weight_frame(
      weight_list[[i]],
      weight_var = weight_var
    )

    stopifnot(
      nrow(weights_i) ==
        expected_parent_n +
        expected_control_n,
      n_distinct(
        weights_i$couple_id
      ) ==
        nrow(
          weights_i
        ),
      all(
        is.finite(
          weights_i$WEIGHT
        )
      ),
      all(
        weights_i$WEIGHT > 0
      )
    )

    analysis_i <- outcome_wide %>%
      inner_join(
        weights_i,
        by = "couple_id"
      )

    stopifnot(
      nrow(
        analysis_i
      ) ==
        expected_parent_n +
        expected_control_n,
      all(
        analysis_i$group ==
          analysis_i$group_weight
      ),
      sum(
        analysis_i$group == 1L
      ) ==
        expected_parent_n,
      sum(
        analysis_i$group == 0L
      ) ==
        expected_control_n
    )

    analysis_i <- analysis_i %>%
      mutate(
        PARENT = group
      )

    mplus_i <- analysis_i %>%
      select(
        couple_id_num,
        PARENT,
        PID_M,
        all_of(
          paste0(
            "M_LS",
            0:7
          )
        ),
        PID_F,
        all_of(
          paste0(
            "F_LS",
            0:7
          )
        ),
        WEIGHT
      )

    stopifnot(
      identical(
        names(
          mplus_i
        ),
        mplus_columns
      )
    )

    # Store outcome-only portion so we can prove outcomes do not vary by
    # imputation. Weight is deliberately excluded from this check.
    exported_outcomes[[i]] <-
      mplus_i %>%
      select(
        -WEIGHT
      )

    file_name <- sprintf(
      "%s_imp%02d.dat",
      specification_name,
      i
    )

    file_path <- file.path(
      out_dir,
      file_name
    )

    write.table(
      mplus_i,
      file = file_path,
      row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = FALSE,
      quote = FALSE,
      sep = " ",
      na = "999"
    )

    file_names[i] <-
      file_name

    parent_w <-
      mplus_i$WEIGHT[
        mplus_i$PARENT == 1L
      ]

    control_w <-
      mplus_i$WEIGHT[
        mplus_i$PARENT == 0L
      ]

    export_diagnostics[[i]] <- tibble(
      specification =
        specification_name,
      imp =
        i,
      n =
        nrow(
          mplus_i
        ),
      n_parent =
        sum(
          mplus_i$PARENT == 1L
        ),
      n_control =
        sum(
          mplus_i$PARENT == 0L
        ),
      parent_weight_min =
        min(
          parent_w
        ),
      parent_weight_max =
        max(
          parent_w
        ),
      control_weight_min =
        min(
          control_w
        ),
      control_weight_median =
        median(
          control_w
        ),
      control_weight_max =
        max(
          control_w
        ),
      n_missing_ls =
        sum(
          is.na(
            mplus_i[
              ,
              c(
                paste0(
                  "M_LS",
                  0:7
                ),
                paste0(
                  "F_LS",
                  0:7
                )
              )
            ]
          )
        )
    )
  }

  # Observed outcome trajectories and IDs must be exactly identical across
  # imputations; only the weights should differ.
  for (i in 2:20) {
    stopifnot(
      identical(
        exported_outcomes[[1]],
        exported_outcomes[[i]]
      )
    )
  }

  # Mplus TYPE=IMPUTATION list file. Because the Mplus .inp will be placed
  # in this same directory, filenames can remain relative.
  list_file <- file.path(
    out_dir,
    paste0(
      specification_name,
      "_list.dat"
    )
  )

  writeLines(
    file_names,
    con = list_file
  )

  # Small text dictionary to make the exported column order explicit.
  writeLines(
    c(
      "Mplus column order:",
      mplus_names_text,
      "",
      "Missing value code: 999",
      "PARENT: 0 = non-parenting control; 1 = parent",
      paste0(
        "Expected couples: ",
        expected_parent_n,
        " parents + ",
        expected_control_n,
        " controls"
      )
    ),
    con = file.path(
      out_dir,
      paste0(
        specification_name,
        "_columns.txt"
      )
    )
  )

  bind_rows(
    export_diagnostics
  )
}
```

## 6. Export locked primary entropy-ATT analysis

```{r}
diag_primary <- export_mplus_imputations(
  weight_list =
    primary_weighted,
  weight_var =
    "att_weight_ebal",
  specification_name =
    "primary_entropy_att",
  expected_parent_n =
    709L,
  expected_control_n =
    893L
)

print(
  diag_primary,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)
```

## 7. Export support-restricted ATT sensitivity

This sensitivity contains the 641 parent couples with `rel_duration <= 5` and all 893 controls.

```{r}
diag_support <- export_mplus_imputations(
  weight_list =
    support_weighted,
  weight_var =
    "weight_sensitivity",
  specification_name =
    "sensitivity_rel5_age2_att",
  expected_parent_n =
    641L,
  expected_control_n =
    893L
)

print(
  diag_support,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)
```

## 8. Export full-sample ATO sensitivity

```{r}
diag_ato <- export_mplus_imputations(
  weight_list =
    ato_weighted,
  weight_var =
    "weight_sensitivity",
  specification_name =
    "sensitivity_ato",
  expected_parent_n =
    709L,
  expected_control_n =
    893L
)

print(
  diag_ato,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)
```

## 9. Cross-specification checks

```{r}
export_diagnostics <- bind_rows(
  diag_primary,
  diag_support,
  diag_ato
)

write_csv(
  export_diagnostics,
  here(
    "data",
    "derived",
    "mplus_export_diagnostics.csv"
  )
)

export_summary <- export_diagnostics %>%
  group_by(
    specification
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    imputations =
      n(),
    n_min =
      min(
        n
      ),
    n_max =
      max(
        n
      ),
    parent_n =
      first(
        n_parent
      ),
    control_n =
      first(
        n_control
      ),
    min_parent_weight =
      min(
        parent_weight_min
      ),
    max_parent_weight =
      max(
        parent_weight_max
      ),
    min_control_weight =
      min(
        control_weight_min
      ),
    max_control_weight =
      max(
        control_weight_max
      ),
    missing_ls_min =
      min(
        n_missing_ls
      ),
    missing_ls_max =
      max(
        n_missing_ls
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(
  export_summary,
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    export_summary$imputations ==
      20L
  ),
  all(
    export_summary$missing_ls_min ==
      export_summary$missing_ls_max
  )
)

cat(
  "\nPASS: all Mplus specifications contain 20 imputations,\n",
  "and the observed LS missingness pattern is identical across imputations.\n",
  sep = ""
)
```
